Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1043 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.
  • It has been revealed that the question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care.
  • Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.

It has been revealed that the question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care. In the US, that shift is reaching hospital standards. From January 2027, breast cancer centers must screen patients' physical function and recommend exercise or physical therapy where needed.

Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.

The 2025 trial, called CHALLENGE, was led by the Canadian Cancer Trials Group. It began enrolling patients in 2009 and published its results in 2025.

The trial's 889 participants came from six countries, most from Canada and Australia. All had finished surgery and chemotherapy for stage 2 or 3 colon cancer, which had not spread to distant organs.

In a recent development, half received only health education materials on exercise and healthy eating. The other half additionally met a physical activity consultant for three years.

Industry observers note that in the exercise group, the target was similar to adding 45 to 60 minutes of brisk walking, three to four times a week. The amount and type of activity varied from person to person, mentioned Tormod Skogstad Nilsen, a cancer exercise researcher in Norway. But he said participants achieved lasting increases in their physical activity.

According to recent reports, exercise helped. People in the exercise group were less likely to see their cancer come back, to develop a upcoming cancer or to die. In all, 93 had at least one of these setbacks, compared with 131 in the health education group.

Recent findings suggest that in cancer research, living longer usually means a larger share of people is still alive at a given point. It does not promise anyone a set number of extra years.

Eight years after joining CHALLENGE, about 90 of every 100 people in the exercise group were alive, compared with about 83 of every 100 in the health education group. That is about 7% more people alive in the group who had guided exercise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that for people without cancer, the evidence comes from studies that follow people's habits and health over many years. These can show a link, but not prove cause and effect. Active people may also eat better or smoke less.

According to recent reports, in another 2025 study, more than 85,000 adults in the United Kingdom wore a wrist tracker for a week. Over about six years, those who moved most had a 26% lower risk of 13 cancers, including breast and colorectal cancer, than those who moved least.

In a recent development, even light activity, such as household chores, was linked to lower risk. The link held after researchers accounted for lifestyle, weight and other health conditions.

According to recent reports, earlier research, based on people's self-reporting, has led to similar conclusions. A 2016 analysis of 1.44 million adults in the US and Europe linked free-time activity to a lower risk of many cancers, largely regardless of weight or smoking.

A trial to prove prevention is unlikely: Many cancers take years to develop, so it would need huge numbers of people followed for a long time.

It has been revealed that CHALLENGE included only people with colon cancer. But how it picked participants offers a clue: Before joining, they had to pass a fitness test.

Anna Campbell, a professor of clinical exercise science at Edinburgh Napier University in Scotland, sees that as a guide.

In a recent development, "I think patients with any other cancer stage II and III who have a reasonable baseline level of fitness and no major comorbidities that would prevent them from undertaking moderate to vigorous activity could be considered for similar interventions," she stated. Comorbidities are other health conditions.

Nilsen noted some people decline to join exercise trials because they feel too unwell or tired, or do not want to exercise. "Hence, study populations are typically younger, 'healthier', and most times slightly more motivated compared to a clinical population," he remarked.

The coaching aimed to make activity a lasting habit, and Campbell said that is where the trial's value lies.

"The main success of the study is that it enabled the participants to become independent exercisers staying active in a safe and effective and individualized way," she said.

According to recent reports, nilsen agreed. Helping people become more active "in their own environment," without depending on a well-equipped training center, "would likely lead to more sustainable activity behavioral changes," he remarked.

In a recent development, he is wary of fixed targets, however. "Exercise should be tailored to each individual and the challenges they face, rather than striving to reach a given minimum of exercise required," though health care resources may not always allow it, he added.

In a 2024 survey of 549 people with cancer, only one in 10 had been referred to an exercise service. Yet almost three in four thought their oncologist should raise the subject.

Industry observers note that "There are some excellent examples of effective pathways but these are few and far between," said Campbell. Good services bring everyone on board, from surgeons to community fitness instructors.

"Ideally, one person in the clinical setting needs to champion the program to link all the team together.".

It has been revealed that campbell expects CHALLENGE's regular coaching will be cut back in everyday care. Apps and live online group sessions could still work, she said, if run by properly trained staff.

One recent study of live online exercise engaged patients from poorer backgrounds, in rural areas and with advanced cancer. "It answered some of the barriers, such as cost, travel and lack of confidence," she said.

Patients can ask their care team what exercise is safe for them and what support exists.

According to Nilsen, a training session can bring structure and company. "You made it here, despite your feeling unwell or fatigued this morning, so you feel mastery based on that," he said.

In just a few months, Donyell Malen has become an absolute focal point for Roma fans and Gian Piero Gasperini’s team.

The Dutch striker knows only one verb: to score. And he does so with a frequency that has surprised even the most optimistic: 27 goals in 34 games for the Giallorossi since he set foot in the capital.

An extraordinary performance that has inevitably attracted the attention of major European teams, with the spotlight shifting from the Premier League substantial names to the Bundesliga.

Several clubs are monitoring Donyell Malen ahead of the summer transfer window, but Roma doesn’t want to be caught off guard.

Industry observers note that roma wants to secure Donyell Malen. As Corriere dello Sport reports, the Giallorossi club, given the striker’s exceptional performances and the resulting interest from major European clubs, is considering a contract renewal with a salary adjustment that recognizes the player’s value.

Bobby had accepted a salary of approximately €3.7 million plus bonuses until 2030, less than the €4.6 million plus €700,000 he earned at Aston Villa.

The agreement was accompanied by a handshake, with the possibility of renegotiating the deal if his performances met expectations.

Malen has kept all his promises, which is why Roma is ready to talk to his entourage about treating him as a top-level center forward.

According to recent reports, the Roman club will offer the born-1999 player a latest salary that will exceed €4 million net, exceeding the current threshold represented by Mile Svilar, who is currently the highest-paid player in the Giallorossi squad. Roma is preparing to secure its striker.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 08:03 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:49 EST, 16 November 2026.

Romelu Lukaku has announced his retirement from international football in a 'bombshell' decision that has left the Belgian press utterly stunned.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United forward, 33, vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team, although he now appears to have changed his mind over his future.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku took to social media on Monday morning to break the unexpected news.

'16 years old,' his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

Industry observers note that 'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'.

Belgium legend Romelu Lukaku has announced his decision to retire from international football.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament.

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench.

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking on the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retires as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

Belgian newspapers were caught out by the shock announcement, which was described as an 'unexpected bombshell' by outlet HLN on Monday.

Lukaku's stock within the international set-up has fallen since he promised the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament in January.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the tournament under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1.

Axel Witsel sent a heartfelt message to Lukaku on Instagram: 'Thanks for everything, legend'.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute - and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

In a recent development, 'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he mentioned.

'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'.

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

The tests revealed a more serious problem than initially thought by Nigeria’s medical staff, raising alarm at the club.

At first, the African national team’s doctors had diagnosed a mild sprain, suggesting a relatively quick recovery time.

However, the assessments carried out by Atlético Madrid have significantly altered the clinical picture. The club’s statement read: “Ademola Lookman has suffered a severe knee sprain during Nigeria’s match against Tanzania on Friday, November 13.”.

The recovery program will begin today, when Lookman will begin his first physiotherapy sessions and rehabilitation work in the gym.

It has been revealed that for a serious sprain, the minimum recovery period is generally estimated at around six weeks, although the actual duration will depend on the knee’s response to treatment. Atlético Madrid will therefore need to carefully monitor the player’s progress, without rushing it.

The possibility that the Nigerian won’t return to action before 2027 is real, given the severity of the injury and the calendar now approaching the end of the calendar year.

Recent findings suggest that roma and sporting director D’Amico remain vigilant ahead of the January transfer window: in addition to their strong support for Endrick, the Giallorossi management is keen to sign Gian Piero Gasperini, and Lookman fits the profile the Grugliasco-born coach is seeking perfectly. In the coming weeks, it will be clearer whether the former Atalanta player’s injury will pose an obstacle to this.

Breaking: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer.
  • It has been revealed that the idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate.
  • "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer. This year, though, the tournament, being hosted by Denmark from November 6 to November 16, is being held in November for the first time.

It has been revealed that the idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate. Since its inception in 2023, the North America-based Professional Women's Hockey League (PWHL), widely considered the world's best, has had to pause its season to allow players to take part in the Worlds. This is no longer necessary, as the PWHL's regular season doesn't open until December.

"This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency. "Because the PWHL season begins after this, we can be certain that the very best players are participating.".

Previously, the teams were divided into a stronger group and a weaker group, with the idea being to avoid, as much as possible, lopsided scores. This is because women's hockey is not as balanced as the men's game, with Canada or the United States having won every tournament since its inception.

Recent findings suggest that under the old system, all five teams in the stronger Group A advanced to the quarterfinals. Under the new format, four of the five teams advance from both groups. This also sees powerhouses the US and Canada in separate groups, meaning the marquee matchup can't occur early in the tournament.

Group A: USA, Czechia, Switzerland, Germany, Austria.

Group B: Canada, Finland, Sweden, Japan, Denmark.

No. While the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on October 30 — a week before the opening faceoff of the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship — that the IIHF must allow Russia back into its tournaments during the 2026-2027 season, it made no mention of this tournament. Under the CAS ruling though, the IIHF will be required to include Russia at the 2027 tournament in Quebec City.

As noted above, either Canada or the United States has won every edition of this tournament — and indeed the two countries have split Olympic gold medals between them (Canada with five, USA with three) since the sport was introduced to the Winter Games in 1998. There is nothing to suggest that this is about to change in Herning and Esbjerg, although Canada enters the tournament with a vastly different roster from the one that won Olympic silver in Milano in February.

Among those looking to break this North American domination are Finland, the only other team ever to have made it to a world championship final and Switzerland, who took bronze in Milan.

The United States and Canada will play in generic kits provided by the International Ice Hockey Federation's official supplier due to an ongoing commercial rights dispute.

The Canadian federation, Hockey Canada, stated in a statement on Wednesday that its players would be wearing jerseys designed by True Hockey instead of their Bauer jerseys featuring the national team logo. USA Hockey has confirmed that its players too will be wearing jerseys without its national emblem.

"While we have yet to see the jersey Canada will be playing in on Friday, our team remains focused on the tournament and representing our country proudly on and off the ice," Hockey Canada noted.

Remembering the night Eden Hazard scored a hungover hat-trick

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When the time came for Eden Hazard to wave goodbye to Lille, his club legend status had long been secured.
  • Hazard had already been a standout player in Lille’s stunning 2010-11 Ligue 1 triumph, the club’s first league title in over 50 years, while his star shone even brighter the following year, finishing as their top scorer with a career-best 22 goals.
  • In a recent development, twenty of those goals came in the league, with a further 16 assists.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When the time came for Eden Hazard to wave goodbye to Lille, his club legend status had long been secured. Needless to say, he wasn’t going out with a whimper.

Hazard had already been a standout player in Lille’s stunning 2010-11 Ligue 1 triumph, the club’s first league title in over 50 years, while his star shone even brighter the following year, finishing as their top scorer with a career-best 22 goals.

In a recent development, twenty of those goals came in the league, with a further 16 assists. Obscene numbers beyond what even Neymar would reach in the French top-flight in later years.

It was obvious that the Belgium international’s talent belonged at one of Europe’s elite clubs.

Sure enough, at the end of the season, he abruptly ended years of protracted tabloid speculation and announced on Twitter that he was joining the champions of Europe, Chelsea.

But while Roberto Di Matteo’s Blues played out that final in Munich, Hazard was still in France, out on the lash one last time with his Lille team-mates.

Recent findings suggest that “We were certain to finish third and we were facing Nancy the following day,” former Lille captain Rio Mavuba later revealed. “It was Eden Hazard’s last match with Lille and he wanted to organise a little something.

In a recent development, “We decided to go have a little drink. A little drink that dragged on somewhat. The following morning, Eden was still drunk. That evening against Nancy, not even with 30 minutes played, Eden had already bagged a hat-trick.”.

There was certainly no sign of a hangover come kick-off, with a boyish grin as he looked out across a packed-out Stadium Lille Metropole – also Lille’s last game there, after an eight-year exile in the out-of-town athletics venue – full of banners reading ‘Merci Eden’ among Belgian flags, showing their love for a 21-year-old who’d already become one of the greatest players in the club’s history.

Brazilian striker Tulio de Melo led the line, while Hazard supported from the right, with Dimitri Payet on the opposite flank, Joe Cole operating in the No.10 role, future PSG man Idrissa Gueye at the base of midfield and 18-year-old academy graduate Lucas Digne making an early appearance at left-back.

It didn’t take that special side long to wreak havoc against midtable Nancy, and the players seemed to revel in the lack of pressure in a game that had more the air of a testimonial. Just like the night before, they were there to enjoy themselves.

According to recent reports, not even 10 minutes had gone by before Hazard was put through after some sublime one-touch interplay between Cole and De Melo in the centre of the park. He made no mistake with his finish.

Stood in a huddle to celebrate, there was some degree of choreography in what appeared to be a less-than-subtle nod – or the opposite, in fact, tilting their heads back to mime necking booze – to the previous night’s antics.

While there was no lack of sharpness in the slick passing or dead-eyed finishing for the opener, some sloppy defending at a set-piece allowed the visitors to get back on level terms within a couple of minutes as Nancy full-back Reynald Lemaitre found himself free to send a glancing head in at the near post.

But Lille weren’t going to allow Hazard’s farewell party to be ruined, and soon enough Payet produced a trademark silky touch to turn his man before nutmegging another Nancy defender to tee up De Melo, who tapped home to regain their lead in the 21st minute.

According to recent reports, nancy had enough to worry about with a young Hazard at the peak of his powers. Facing an in-the-mood Payet as well? That’s just cruel.

READ: When Joe Cole, Eden Hazard & Dimitri Payet lived out my football dream.

With a lead restored and the pouring rain failing to dampen the party atmosphere, Lille sniffed blood and swiftly put Nancy to the sword.

Having received the ball just outside the centre circle, Payet exhibited another string to his bow, by sending a looping through ball over the top of Nancy’s backline.

The alcohol in his system evidently hadn’t dulled Hazard’s attacking instincts, given he was on his toes to read the pass and dart into the empty space for a second time in just half an hour.

If you’re the wrong side of 30, chances are you’ll look back wistfully on your 21-year-old self’s ability to shake off the after-effects of a heavy night as if it were a mild cold.

Chances are you wouldn’t have been able to time your run, casually control a ball arriving over your shoulder, before showing enough composure to slot it past an onrushing goalkeeper. That’s just showing off.

After just 34 minutes, the Belgian was gifted a golden chance to score his third when Payet was clipped in the area.

According to recent reports, as with his first two gilt-edged chances, it never felt like a possibility that he could miss. Not on that night.

After he completed his first-half hat-trick, De Melo lifted Hazard onto his shoulders to celebrate, showing his gratitude to the best player he’d ever play alongside, and “a very good boy – but a bit debauched,” as he later told Goal.

— EiF (@EiFSoccer) July 31, 2023.

Hazard had assured a perfect send-off, and he’d done it with an hour to spare. The game drifted from there, with all that needed to be done out of the way promptly.

But there was still a chance for the fans to properly show their appreciation to their half-drunk hero, as Lille boss Rudi Garcia introduced Mavuba in his place in injury time.

After embracing each of his team-mates, Hazard trudged off the turf at Lille one last time, reciprocating his standing ovation by applauding the supporters in response.

“The guy had not even slept, he drank for the entire night and he put away a hat-trick in [just over] 30 minutes,” his substitute recalled.

“We all looked at each other, we told ourselves that this guy was the real deal.”.

Published: 08:02 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 10:36 EST, 16 November 2026.

Jurgen Klopp has called on FIFA's embattled president Gianni Infantino to resign, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

Infantino's reputation took a nosedive after his sycophantic behaviour towards Donald Trump before and during the World Cup - most memorably by awarding him a 'FIFA Peace Prize'.

And it only got worse when his clandestine plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup, a devious scheme which would have banked him millions, was revealed by The Times.

Now Germany manager Klopp has hit out: 'There is now a unanimous consensus that a change would make sense.

'I thought that, after Sepp Blatter, the situation couldn't get any worse - but here we are.

'Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.

Jurgen Klopp has publicly savaged FIFA president Gianni Infantino, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

The Germany manager noted Infantino - who tried to sell off stakes in the World Cup to his own benefit - is 'worse' than his predecessor Sepp Blatter.

'Without a doubt, there are people who truly care about football and have no financial interests,' the former Liverpool manager mentioned.

Infantino has clung on to his job thus far, surviving a crisis summit in Morocco in August, despite intense and widespread opposition.

A total of 90 nations including all of UEFA's teams rebelled, with threats to boycott FIFA competitions, and Infantino's £3.1billion strategy fell apart.

But he still maintained a large swell of support among Africa, Asia, and South America - especially after offering each nation £30million if they supported his blueprint. His opponents pointed out that he could simply have given money from FIFA's cash reserves of roughly £4.5b.

In the pages of this historic newspaper, football legend Luis Figo wrote that 'Infantino must go' and accused him of 'debasing the office of FIFA President'.

FIFA does not have a history of picking good leaders - Blatter resigned in 2015 amid allegations of corruption, though he was cleared alongside Michel Platini last year.

Infantino now looks well-placed to be re-elected for a fourth term in next March's presidential elections.

The deadline for candidacies to be submitted is November 18.

Philippe Diallo, the French Football Federation president, has agreed to run against Infantino and has the backing of UEFA's executive committee.

'(Diallo has) extensive experience across all levels of the game, having led the organisation representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of the French professional league and within FIFA’s dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and a member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023,' UEFA mentioned.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has already announced his intention to be a rival to Infantino.

Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, is also reportedly set to mount a challenge.

Ex-Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger was touted as a potential challenger but it is understood he told European football’s governing body UEFA that he would not stand.

Sunil Chhetri is a name you are probably not familiar with but he is a legend of Indian football.

He is the all-time top scorer in Indian Super League history, the most capped and top scorer for his nation and the fourth-highest goalscorer in international football history.

He played for India from 2005 to 2025, a two-decade-long career that saw him score 95 goals in 157 games.

His playing career was largely in his home country but he did briefly sign for Kansas City Wizards in 2010.

The Argentine great retired from international duty this year, bringing an end to a career which began in 2005.

While he famously scored on his Barcelona debut, it did not go so well for the national team with a red card in his first match. Perhaps disheartened by that, it took Messi six games to get on the scoresheet for Argentina.

Messi was actually quite slow going for his country to begin with, in contrast to how he was with Barcelona, leading to accusations from some that he never performed for his international team but that all changed from the 2014 World Cup.

Four goals in the tournament in which he pretty much dragged Argentina to the final kick-started a Messi era of ridiculous goalscoring.

In the most recent World Cup, he scored eight before his final goal for his nation in a friendly against Benin.

Considering the goalscoring form he is in, this feels like a ratio that is only going to improve in the next few years.

Mbappe has scored 67 goals for France, including four in major finals, in 108 games for Les Bleues.

Now playing as the number nine in a stacked French squad, you would fancy him to get even more goals in the next few years.

Ranking the 10 best strikers in world football right now: Mbappe, Kane or Haaland top?

Neymar was just 18 years old when he scored his first goal for Brazil and he was scoring at a ridiculous rate in his early career.

By the end of the following year, Neymar had already scored eight goals for Brazil and was well on his way to becoming one of Brazil’s best scorers of all time.

That title did eventually come in 2023 when Neymar surpassed Pele, although the Brazilian great had a far superior goal-to-game ratio at 0.84.

Ronaldo is the top scorer in international history and was not slow in getting to that number.

It took 234 games for the Portuguese talisman to reach 146, putting him at a goal-to-game ratio of 0.62 which is the fourth best amongst players still in the game.

Ronaldo has retired now but his record will take some beating.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United forward does love a goal for his country.

He’s got 94 of them, putting him miles ahead of second-place Kevin De Bruyne on 41, and Lukaku is the fifth top scorer in international history.

He announced his international retirement this month but still plays club football for Fenerbahce.

The England captain has really picked up the pace of late for both club and country goals and has 93 in 127 for the Three Lions.

Kane passed Wayne Rooney to become England’s top goalscorer in 2023 and it has taken him just three years to add another 39 to his tally.

The most recent Ballon d’Or winner looks to have at least another Euros in him if not one more World Cup so has a chance to add plenty more to his tally.

His 96th-minute winner against Scandinavian neighbours Denmark was the 68th goal of his Norwegian career and he has reached that mark in just 61 games.

That is easily the best goal-to-game ratio of any active player and puts him third in the all-time list of players who have scored over 50 goals.

He is behind only Poul Nielsen of Denmark and Vivian Woodward of England but both of those played pre-WWII and so Haaland is the best of the modern era.

His goals have powered Norway to the quarter-finals of the Nations League with the country yet to win an international honour of any kind.

Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.
  • About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.
  • It is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.

About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.

It is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK). And it's been up and running for more than two decades.

The first LÜKEX in 2004 dealt with the scenario of an extreme winter with a major power outage. Lessons from that exercise proved valuable in 2005 when the Münsterland region of North Rhine-Westphalia — Germany's most populous state — experienced the worst power outage in the country's postwar history. When heavy snowfall caused power lines to collapse, leaving 250,000 people without electricity for days, there was a better understanding of who to contact and where the bottlenecks were.

Industry observers note that since it first started, LÜKEX has trained for scenarios involving terror attacks, an influenza pandemic, biological health threats, storm floods in northern Germany and gas shortages in southern Germany. The most recent exercise in 2023 simulated a cyberattack targeting government operations.

With the help of other ministries, the German Weather Service and the Federal Institute of Hydrology, the BBK developed a drought risk analysis to serve as the scenario.

Participants, which include aid organizations Malteser and the German Red Cross, didn't know the specifics of the challenges they would be facing until the exercise kicked off on Wednesday.

Industry observers note that at that point, they were told it was July 20, 2027. In that simulated future, they find themselves in a Germany that has been struggling with extreme heat for weeks; water levels in rivers are falling, food supplies are becoming scarce and emergency services are under growing pressure.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that patrick Pöhler, spokesperson for Malteser, noted additional details include supermarkets having run out of water, collapsed supply chains and skyrocketing prices to enter a swimming pool. He said the scenario also goes into how the situation is impacting sections of society.

"Emergency services and elderly care are areas that require particular attention," Pöhler said. "The increasingly extreme summers of recent years have shown how severely heat can affect staffing levels and operational capacity.".

In its scenario, the northern port city of Hamburg is tasked with managing the disruption of key transport routes that are impacting access to food and drinking water, as well as handling disinformation attacks that are fueling public fear.

Recent findings suggest that "We have not conducted an exercise of this magnitude since the end of the Cold War. Yet such preparations are essential to strengthen our resilience and crisis-response capabilities," said Hamburg's minister for the interior, Andy Grote.

Industry observers note that LÜKEX is designed to test and strengthen the country's ability to manage major crises at a strategic level. No matter the specific scenario, they all help test internal structures, workflows and decision-making processes.

"The lessons learned are continuously incorporated into improving preparedness, planning and cooperation in civil protection," said BBK spokesperson Katharina Böcker.

Recent findings suggest that this year's topic was decided a long time ago, well before recent summers in which Germany experienced extreme heat, she added. Thousands of people died from heat-related causes during the hot months of this year.

"Crises such as extreme heat waves and prolonged droughts can affect large parts of the population and challenge the operational capabilities of our critical structures over an extended period," mentioned Christian Reuter, secretary general of the German Red Cross, another organization taking part.

Observers take note of how organizations react in the crisis scenario to find out what went well and where things didn't run smoothly.

"We are explicitly encouraged to make mistakes," remarked Malteser's Pöhler, because that is how weaknesses can be identified and addressed.

A first internal debrief is scheduled for Friday, he added.

A preliminary report with the main findings and respective recommendations is due to be published in the first quarter of next year. A full evaluation report will then be released later in the third quarter of 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jordan Pickford edged closer to a century of caps for the England national team on Thursday evening, with James Garner also featuring in a 2-1 victory over Croatia that booked passage to the UEFA Nations League quarter-final stage.

Confirmed by Thomas Tuchel as England’s continuing number one at the start of the international break, Pickford started at Wembley in his 94th senior Three Lions outing.

According to recent reports, the spotlight for the evening, however, was firmly on Harry Kane. The Bayern Munich striker was fresh from picking up the Ballon D’Or and made yet more history by surpassing Peter Shilton’s long-held record of 125 England appearances.

Garner and Jarrad Branthwaite, meanwhile, were both on the bench, but only the former would take to the field.

By the time Tuchel made a triple substitution in the 77nd minute – with Garner replacing Arsenal captain Declan Rice in midfield – Kane had already restored England’s lead.

Morgan Rogers had given the hosts the advantage with a close-range finish in the first half, but an error from defender Jarrell Quansah allowed the Croatians to level on the hour mark.

Kane then converted from the spot five minutes later, before it looked to be a dream cameo from Garner as he found the back of the net himself, but a VAR check confirmed an offside in the build-up to deny a first senior international goal for Everton's 2025/26 Player of the Season.

Branthwaite remained an unused substitute in London and will be hoping for game time when England head to Madrid to take on World and European champions Spain in their final game in Group C.

But while the jury remains out on whether they’ll get back on their pedestal over the next few years, there’s one thing they can take encouragement from: they’ve found a striker.

It’s been a problem position for Italy for years. The most recent goal by a member of their top 10 scorers of all time was back in 2007. No one has really made a dent on the list since.

There’s been strikers like Ciro Immobile tearing it up in Serie A who could never really do it at international level. Just the 17 goals over nine years for him, of which just three were at tournaments. Andrea Belotti, you ask? 12 goals; one at a tournament.

But now there might be light at the end of the tunnel in Italy’s striker search. The 21-year-old Inter talent Esposito scored a brace against France and the opener against Belgium.

He’s now up to 10 goals for his country, overtaking the likes of Francesco Totti, Fabio Quagliarella and Stephan El Shaarawy and going level with Gianfranco Zola.

Let’s not get ahead of ourselves too much here, but Italy’s all-time scoring record is only 35 goals, set by Luigi Riva. Esposito is only 21 years old and could quite easily smash that if he stays injury free.

A bona fide Nations League success story. We all remember a time when Faroe Islands were whipping boys in qualifiers for major tournaments. But the tide is turning.

They already won as many games as they lost in their unlikely attempt to reach the last World Cup, finishing third in their group – behind Croatia and the Czech Republic, but above Montenegro and Gibraltar.

Now they’re a play-off tie away from promotion to the dizzy heights of League B in the Nations League.

Securing second place in their group behind Slovakia with a 1-0 win over Moldova on Monday, Faroe Islands are a national team on the up.

Recent findings suggest that they’ll find out on Friday who their opponents will be for the March play-offs. It’ll either be Israel, Romania, Georgia or North Macedonia, and that’s maybe not so daunting for them these days. There’s a scenario where they end up in the same Nations League tier as Turkey, Poland and Croatia.

We’re starting to suspect Liverpool Florian Wirtz and Germany Florian Wirtz are actually two different people.

Sources indicate that three goals in two games for the attacking midfielder, including a brace in the crucial 5-0 win over the Netherlands to secure top spot. He’s got three goals in his last 19 games for Liverpool, in contrast.

It has been revealed that A confidence boost he can use to kick on at club level? Maybe, but we’ve been here before.

He has seven goals for Germany in 2026, just one fewer than he has for Liverpool in the same time.

Recent findings suggest that more than one German media source described his impact against the Netherlands as magical. Andoni Iraola will be hoping to find the same potion.

What a comeback that was, by the way.

It was practically a straight shootout between Norway and Denmark for second place in their group and progression to the quarter-finals. And things weren’t looking good for Norway when Denmark went 2-0 up inside a quarter of an hour.

But then Haaland happened. As he does. He pulled one back before half time and then it was over to Martin Odegaard to level things up in the last 10 minutes.

Sources indicate that A draw still wasn’t enough for Norway, so up stepped Haaland to clinch a smash-and-grab win with a 96th-minute penalty. Boom.

It’s easy to forget this was Norway’s first Nations League campaign at this level. Now they’re in the final eight.

Sources indicate that scored an outrageous free kick for Turkey. Signed a new contract with Real Madrid. Been a pretty good couple of weeks for this guy.

Sources indicate that norway’s ecstasy was Denmark’s despair. Conceding a stoppage-time penalty to miss out on the quarter-finals must hurt, especially on home turf and with how they started the game.

According to recent reports, all this after a convincing 4-1 win over Portugal as well. Now they’re in the relegation play-offs. Ouch.

We were intrigued heading into this international break over the prospect of Germany or the Netherlands being a big casualty from League A if they were to fall into the relegation play-off.

It was Greece who started this month at the top of their group, but things unravelled fast.

Industry observers note that A 7-0 thumping by the Netherlands was brutal. Even Tijjani Reijnders scored a hat-trick. The damage was done; even after a 1-0 win over Serbia, they came out third best in the combined head-to-head table with the three sides who finished on 11 points.

It was so close that even that head-to-head table was separated only by goal difference. Needless to say, the massive swing in the Netherlands thrashing did them no favours at all.

In a recent development, we’ve actually been quite impressed by Anderson so far this season. Almost everyone expected him to crumble under the weight of expectations at Manchester City due to that transfer fee, but he’s holding his own.

Recent findings suggest that he’s also establishing himself as an England regular. He was a winner last time we did this. But he can do without lapses of judgement like against Spain.

When England were 3-0 up, Anderson got a straight red card for denying a goalscoring opportunity by pulling back Lamine Yamal. It was needless and could have been costly, with Spain threatening a comeback once they had the numerical advantage.

Anderson will probably keep featuring prominently in England lineups in 2027 and beyond, but he’ll need to cut stuff like that out.

We can cut Cubarsi some slack for his struggles against England as he was carrying a hip problem that forced him off at half time.

Industry observers note that but he isn’t getting off that lightly. The Barcelona defender was to blame for Spain going behind, giving away a penalty by clumsily fouling Harry Kane.

It has been revealed that we still think he’s brilliant. But for those who might not watch him regularly, it wasn’t a great impression.

What a difference three days makes. The Netherlands felt on top of the world after their 7-0 whooping of Greece. Less so after their 5-0 humiliation by Germany.

Industry observers note that as we’ve addressed, it doesn’t matter too much. They’re into the quarter-finals. But not without suffering their heaviest ever competitive defeat.

Unsurprisingly, their defenders have been in the firing line. Their back four against Germany consisted of Denzel Dumfries, Jan Paul van Hecke, Micky van de Ven and Jurrien Timber. They’ve received little sympathy.

#25288. Pressing with intensity, getting runners beyond Kane and playing like a 'Premier League team': How Thomas Tuchel's newly introduced-look England dismantled Spain - and what he's learned from cowardly retreat against Argentina

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1606 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Pressing with intensity, getting runners beyond Kane and playing like a 'Premier League team': How Thomas Tuchel's newly introduced-look England dismantled Spain - and what he's learned from cowardly retreat against Argentina

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • By the end of the World Cup, it felt as if Argentina had ripped the mask off Thomas Tuchel’s England only to reveal Gareth Southgate’s England standing there blinking right back at them.
  • On the biggest stage, against the biggest teams, under the biggest pressure, England wilted as they always did.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026.

By the end of the World Cup, it felt as if Argentina had ripped the mask off Thomas Tuchel’s England only to reveal Gareth Southgate’s England standing there blinking right back at them.

On the biggest stage, against the biggest teams, under the biggest pressure, England wilted as they always did. They sat back, they were too cautious, and they lost. And yet, ever since, Tuchel has turned England into a free-scoring winning machine, topped off by a famous victory in Madrid, ending Spain’s 43-match unbeaten streak.

In the six games since the summer, England have scored 19 goals and conceded six. Five of those have been against the world champions.

Yes, this was the Nations League and not a World Cup semi-final. No, it wasn’t at the end of a gruelling five weeks of heat, humidity and altitude. And, yes, it was only a terrific late double save from James Trafford that stopped this being yet another tale of self-sabotaging England, thanks to Elliot Anderson’s red card, blowing another lead when under pressure.

In a recent development, but, this time, England did see it out. They secured Tuchel’s biggest win as England boss and, in doing so, showed us just how he’s been able to get his side playing his way.

Harry Kane leads the England celebrations after his side's victory over Spain in Madrid on Sunday night.

Remember when everyone used to lose their minds whenever Harry Kane dropped deep in major games under Southgate? He’s our bloody striker, for goodness sake. Get in the box!

After England’s defeat by Spain in the Euro 2024 final two years ago, Opta posted on X that Kane had touched the ball just once in the opposition box across both that game and their previous final heartbreak against Italy three years earlier.

‘One fewer than Jack Grealish,’ the post continued. ‘Grealish played 21 minutes in the 2020 final and didn't make the Euro 2024 squad.’.

According to recent reports, ballon d’Or winner Kane has made it quite clear since that he doesn’t need to spend all his time in the box to influence games. When he drops deeper, Kane is able to show the full extent of his creativity and range of passing.

The main problem with the ploy under Southgate, however, was that Kane rarely had the team-mates to make the right runs ahead of him. He was surrounded by players who wanted to take up similar positions. Just look at the average position maps (below) from England’s loss to Spain at Euro 2024 compared to last night.

The average position map of England’s players in the loss to Spain at Euro 2024 show how Kane dropped deep, without team-mates making runs for him to exploit.

...whereas on Sunday night he had runners - Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers - around and beyond him.

Two years ago, the only player who averaged their touches ahead of Kane was Bukayo Saka. Jude Bellingham was out wide. Kobbie Mainoo and Phil Foden were basically in Kane’s shadow.

On Sunday night, he had Anthony Gordon, the brilliant, belligerent Bellingham and Morgan Rogers all ahead of him – and nearly even Ben White.

That desire, and instruction, to flock forward under Tuchel has made such a difference.

Take England’s third goal (below). Kane has the ball outside the area. Rogers is bombing on to his left. Gordon, who started as a winger but finds himself occupying the central spaces Kane leaves behind, darts into the box and points to where he wants it.

According to recent reports, bellingham is demanding the ball, too, showing Kane he wants it to feet. Even Anderson is charging into the box. Kane finds Bellingham, who feeds the unseen White, sprinting forward on the overlap to finish.

Kane picks up the ball and is met with an array of options in front of him, ahead of England's third goal.

He did similar in the win against Croatia a few days earlier, too.

Kane collects the ball deep with four bodies ahead of him, including full backs Lewis Hall and Trent Alexander-Arnold.

It his raking pass to the back post which allows Bellingham to set up Rogers to finish.

Kane's lofted pass to Rogers (top right) leads to a goal against Croatia for Bellingham (edge of box).

Sources indicate that england’s fluidity in the final third is bamboozling defences. That is how you get the best of Kane’s creativity.

PLAYING LIKE A PREMIER LEAGUE SIDE.

Football is changing, so Pep Guardiola told us all in January last year. The modern game is now how teams like Bournemouth and Brighton play. The current Premier League table would suggest he had a point.

Over the past few years in the English top flight, we have seen teams move away from an obsession with keeping the ball for the sake of it and turn towards a far faster, more aggressive and more physical style of play.

Recent findings suggest that tuchel wants to take from that playbook. ‘We're at our best when we're free, physically overpowering and making it Premier League-level,’ remarked Kane after last month's 7-0 rout of Croatia.

In the six matches since the World Cup, Tuchel’s England are having much less of the ball than they did at the start of his reign – and now less even than under Southgate.

The key is they are becoming ever more direct with it. Tuchel wants his England to play out of the back with short passes, entice opponents on to them, but then move it through the lines at speed.

It has been revealed that since the World Cup, England are playing far fewer passes, but more of them into the box – to find those runners. A higher percentage of them forward. More direct attacks, moving the ball up the field at a quicker speed.

In a recent development, on Sunday night, they showed how Tuchel wants his side to press. ‘We were hungry in the opposition half,’ remarked the England boss at full time.

A fine example of that (below) came just after just six minutes. Declan Rice gives his Arsenal team-mate Martín Zubimendi no time at all on the ball inside his own area, charging him down, and forcing him to play out to another Gunner in Mikel Merino. But he, too, is being harassed by Anderson and eventually England win it back and set up Kane for a chance that he fizzes wide.

A half-fit Rice was unable to apply that pressure in the summer.

Declan Rice charges forward to close down Martin Zubimendi who has possession just inside the Spanish box with Kane and Bellingham already engaged in a high press...

...Zubimendi passes to Mikel Merino but Elliot Anderson is all over him and it leads to Kane shot that just fizzes wide.

So much of this improvement under Tuchel into a side capable of blowing teams away can be put down to another abstract word he used post-match in Madrid: ‘brave’.

Tuchel talked in the last international break of ‘unlocking the next level’, and taking ‘calculated risks’ with a ‘man-to-man’ press in the opposition half.

Under Southgate, and certainly in the cowardly retreat against Argentina in the summer, England indicated little bravery either with the ball or without it and frequently showed too much respect to those big nations.

Too safe with the ball, too afraid to give it away, and too fearful to try to win it back in case you leave yourself open.

In a recent development, that appears to be changing, too. There was a moment at the start of the second half when Bellingham tried a risky through-ball to Rogers, which failed to find its man, instead of another simple ball out wide.

It handed Spain possession cheaply. But England didn’t care because they just pounced again. Spain couldn’t deal with it. In the first half, Spain completed just 84 per cent of their passes in their own half – a place where they are usually able to knock it about at will – their lowest completion rate according to Opta since the 2010 World Cup. They didn’t have a shot on target until the penalty.

England’s defence has long been seen as the weak spot and, under Southgate, it felt as though he always would rather his attacking talents not be too frivolous for fear of exposing it.

Thomas Tuchel and Kane direct England's players to keep on the front foot during the win over Spain.

According to recent reports, tuchel is doing the opposite. England’s expected goals soared from 1.7 per game under Southgate from the 2022 World Cup to the end of his reign, to 2.2 under Tuchel’s until this summer’s tournament. Since then, it’s jumped again to 2.8 but at the cost of what they are conceding. In his early days, England coughed up fewer good chances than under Southgate but since the World Cup has more than doubled.

He will want to get that down, of course, but when you are creating so much – and have an array of top finishers to see them off – how much will that matter to Tuchel?

Recent findings suggest that even he’s getting braver. His decision to take off Gordon for Konsa and chuck as many defenders on during England’s shrinking against Argentina looked a decision that would forever haunt Tuchel’s tenure.

Against Spain, Kane made way but Tuchel ended the game with striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin on the pitch. Against Spain, he held his nerve.

#25286. Breaking: Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say
