37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1372 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border.
  • Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.
  • To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border. Yet, 37 years later, many people on both sides remain deeply skeptical of each other.

Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

We asked three artists from Germany with different perspectives on the history of the country's division to share their views.

Author Lea Streisand was born in 1979 and experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall firsthand while growing up in East Berlin.

In her books and essays, she has returned to her East German upbringing many times, using literature to process it.

The novel "Hufeland, at the corner of Bötzow" (2019, Ullstein), for example, recounts the period of reunification from a child's perspective.

In a recent development, "November 9, 1989, was simply incredible," she told DW. She was 10 years old at the time. When her mother bought her winter boots with the 100 Deutsche Marks she received from the West German state — a welcome gift given to all East German citizens — she was so disappointed that she felt like crying. But later, a friend of her parents' let her buy so many sweets at the supermarket that they lasted until Christmas.

Sources indicate that "The disappointment really set in afterwards, with what happened over the course of the following year. It was unbelievable how promptly an entire system was suddenly swept away and a new one built up, as if to say, 'There you go. You're welcome'," Streisand recalled. "I think it was just too fast for people.".

According to recent reports, the people of East Germany, or the GDR, had brought about the fall of the Berlin Wall themselves through a civil rights movement and numerous demonstrations. For many, however, the goal was not to dissolve the state immediately but to reform it.

Sources indicate that among them was Anke Feuchtenberger, born in 1963 in East Berlin. Her childhood was spent in East Berlin and in the East German region of Western Pomerania, where she now lives again and feels "very much at home.".

Today, she teaches at the University of Applied Sciences in Hamburg, meaning she spends time on both sides of the former divide. Feuchtenberger is often described as Germany's most influential comic artist. Her work has also garnered international acclaim.

"Back then, as artists, we tried to bring about a change through posters and flyers — to gain more freedom without immediately abolishing socialism," she explained.

Sources indicate that at the time, the fall of the Berlin Wall stirred up mixed feelings in Feuchtenberger: "I soon realized that the creative and revolutionary aspects of our movement were very swiftly being smothered by consumerism, and that nationalist tendencies — which had already been noticeable before — were coming to the fore," Feuchtenberger recalled. "That made me afraid.".

According to recent reports, meanwhile, for photographic artist Simon Menner, born in 1978 in Emmendingen, in the West German state of Baden-Württemberg, Berlin was very far away. As Menner put it, he experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall as a child in a "rather abstract" way. Today, Berlin is his home.

According to recent reports, in his experience, the way films and documentaries portrayed East Germany around the time of reunification was very bleak. "But West Germany in the '80s," he noted, "was also bleak and very staid.".

This uneven portrayal of the two parts of Germany is an problem that deeply concerns Menner — partly because he unwittingly contributed to it in a small way. Among other things, Menner's work explores the topic of surveillance and how it works.

In the archives of East Germany's Ministry for State Security, or Stasi — which are freely accessible today as part of the National Archives — he discovered a massive collection of photographs that both fascinated and horrified him and which he wanted to bring to the attention of a wider public.

In a recent development, his photo book "Top Secret" (2012, from publisher Hatje Cantz) features a selection of photos that offer a unique insight into the work of the Stasi. Some are eerie, while others are curious or even absurd.

Menner also tried to look into the photo archive of West Germany's Federal Intelligence Service. "I spent a year trying to gain access — without success," he remarked.

In hindsight, he now finds his artistic project problematic because he believes it is too one-sided, focusing exclusively on East Germany's past.

Industry observers note that according to Menner, West Germany's intelligence services in the 1960s were not exactly models of virtue either, and he believes it is "actually high time" to critically examine this part of history as well. In his view, an honest examination of Germany's past as a whole is a prerequisite for genuine reconciliation.

According to recent reports, streisand believes literature can help foster mutual understanding. "Literature opens a window into experiences we haven't had ourselves," she mentioned. "You can immerse yourself in the mind of someone who has had a different life than you have and understand what happened.".

Interest in these stories remains strong. In 2023, Feuchtenberger published the nearly 500-page graphic novel "Comrade Cuckoo" (published by Reprodukt), which was the first graphic novel to be nominated for the Leipzig Book Fair Prize in the fiction category.

In a recent development, the story spans a childhood in the fictional East German village of Pritschitanow in the 1960s in the GDR to the post-Reunification era. In it, Feuchtenberger weaves autobiographical memories of her upbringing with fantastical and fictional elements.

The artist said she was surprised "that, so long after the fall of the wall, my stories have sparked such great interest in the West.".

In particular, the fact that the main character, Kerstin, rarely sees her parents because they both work full-time is a topic that often comes up at readings. In the GDR, everyone had the right to work, she said. At the same time, it was a civic duty.

It has been revealed that could the West German interest in this stem from the fact that full-time employment for both parents has long been less common in the West? It's possible, mentioned Feuchtenberger.

When looking toward their shared future, the two East German women are more optimistic than Menner, from West Germany.

Sources indicate that "In Berlin, I often don't even notice anymore whether I'm in the West or the East," noted Menner. "But when it comes to sociopolitical issues, politicians should listen to older and younger people more closely," he added, referring to the recent election successes of far-right Alternative for Germany, or AfD . "Otherwise, things are going to get difficult in the near future.".

Industry observers note that "It's very important to step outside our own bubble because people all over the world are facing problems. Constantly focusing on this German-German divide that has emerged between the groups doesn't help," noted Feuchtenberger.

Sources indicate that "For me personally, the whole issue of borders has somehow dissolved," she explained. This is due in no small part to the many trips abroad that have taken her to various places around the world.

Sources indicate that moreover, in her hometown near the Polish border, she observes how animals couldn't care less about the border. "They come from the east and the west and do whatever they want," she noted. That's why she also gave "Comrade Cuckoo" the working title "A German Animal in a German Forest," "because I found the absurdity of an animal having a nationality so funny.".

"This East-West thing — our children won't have any interest in it at all," said Streisand. "Young people don't care where their parents come from. Can I get a job that will support a family? Do I have to go to war? Right now, completely different things are relevant.".

This article was originally written in German.

Ruby Mace grabbed the Player of the Match award in the capital – the midfielder repeating her award-winning performance at the home of the North Londoners last term.

In a recent development, it was the visitors who created the first real opportunity inside 17 minutes as Ornella Vignola teed the in-form Yuka Momiki on the edge of the area. The forward, who netted a hat-trick in the 6-0 win in midweek, looked to curl past Lize Kop, but saw her placed effort saved by the diving keeper.

History repeated itself only ten minutes later as Momiki saw another strike palmed away by the keeper. The 30-year-old drifted inside from the right and let fly upon reaching the edge of the box. Unfortunately, Kop anticipated the shot and collected after initially spilling the ball.

Recent findings suggest that the hosts responded on 39 minutes as Courtney Brosnan was called in to action to deny Julie Blakstad. After breaching the Blues’ box, the Norwegian feinted before unleashing a rising strike at goal. Brosnan leapt up to tip the ball over the upright, though.

That concluded the action for a tight, physical opening 45; with Blakstad coming close once more five minutes after the interval.

Found at the back-post, the winger fired at goal and seemed destined to get on the scoresheet. However, Hannah Blundell burst forward to narrow the angle and bravely block, evading the danger.

At the other end, Everton caught Spurs on the break after Momiki held the ball up well on the halfway line. Clare Wheeler threaded it through to the advancing Vignola, who raced at goal with the ball at her feet. She pulled the trigger when faced one-on-one with Kop, but saw her low-strike sail agonisingly wide of the far-post.

It has been revealed that brosnan produced another fine stop five minutes later, the keeper denying Cathinka Tandenberg on this occasion. The Norway-international got down low in an attempt to nestle the ball in to the bottom right corner. Somehow, Brosnan reacted rapidly to palm it away for a corner.

Industry observers note that moments later, Blakstad threatened again – the forward rattling the upright on this occasion. She cut-in past Rosa van Gool and let fly, the ball striking the frame of the goal on its way out.

Head coach Scott Phelan made his first change of the game with 12 minutes remaining as Noemie Mouchon, who scored a brace against Durham on Wednesday, replaced Momiki.

The striker almost had an instant impact as she forced Kop in to a smart save. Rion Ishikawa did brilliantly down the unfamiliar right to dance past two challenges before chipping it through to the substitute. Mouchon came inside before unleashing a curling effort that was caught well by the retreating Kop.

The France-youth international came even closer in the dying minutes as she had a chance similar to Vignola previously. Like her teammate, Mouchon’s strike whistled just wide of the far-post from the right-hand side of the box.

The referee then concluded the affair, with attention now turning to Everton’s Players Cup tie with Manchester United on Wednesday night (7pm KO).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant.
  • The move, which has yet to be publicly confirmed by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play.
  • The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow released its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant. This comes after the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association noted the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) had said it had been removed from the tournament so that Russia could take part.

The move, which has yet to be publicly confirmed by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play. The World Juniors is the first tournament affected by the CAS decision.

The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow released its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In a statement issued Saturday, the IIHF remarked it was "taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization's financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey.".

Recent findings suggest that as of Monday, the IIHF website still listed Norway as one of the participants in the World Juniors, which is to be hosted by Edmonton and Red Deer, Alberta, beginning on December 26. But Swiss Ice Hockey has responded to Norway's statement, saying its team would not face Russia at the World Juniors — as would be the case if it replaces Norway in the schedule.

However, it's far from certain that Russia will actually be able to ice a team in the tournament, as just last week, the Canadian prime minister ruled out the possibility.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," mentioned Mark Carney.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there.".

It has been revealed that how this circle could be squared is unclear. Carney's pledge, coupled with the stated refusal by Finland, Sweden, Switzerland and others to face Russia in an international tournament, appears to have given the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association (NIHF) hope that its team could still play in the upcoming tournament. Several long-time corporate sponsors have also threatened to pull out if Russia is allowed to compete.

"This makes us hope that the last word has not been mentioned about our participation in Canada in December," said NIHF General Secretary Petter Salsten.

"The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association is awaiting further information from the IIHF in the coming days.".

Meanwhile, the German Ice Hockey Association (DEB) is still in discussions with the government in Berlin and the IIHF about how to proceed — or not — with hosting the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in May.

Recent findings suggest that "We intend to host the world championship in Germany next year, and I am very optimistic that we will succeed in doing so," DEB chairman Frank H. Lutz told German broadcaster MagentaSport on Saturday.

While he acknowledged the IIHF's CAS-ordered requirement to include Russia and reiterated the DEB's rejection of the court ruling, he provided no indication as to how this obstacle could be overcome.

Lutz, who said he would be in Berlin for more consultations this week, had previously said handing back Germany's hosting rights was a possibility — if only as a last resort.

On Friday, government spokesman Stefan Kornelius remarked Berlin supports the DEB's efforts to find a solution.

"However, given the boycotts that would follow Russia's readmission, that would effectively be impossible. For this reason, we intend to explore, through dialogue, how we can still ensure the tournament takes place.".

Asked at the same press conference whether Germany could issue visas to a Russian team for the tournament, a Foreign Ministry spokesman indicated that this would be difficult under restrictions currently in place.

"At a time when Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no 'normalcy' — and we will certainly not pretend that there is," remarked spokesperson Martin Giese.

However, he did not categorically rule out the possibility.

It has been suggested that government officials could be choosing their words carefully out of concern for Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

The thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees who are bidding to host an Olympic Games — like the German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB) — to follow its lead.

Asked whether the debate over Russia's possible involvement in a hockey tournament could affect Munich's chances, government spokesman Kornelius mentioned he didn't wish to "speculate on implications.".

Still, with the IOC set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process, one has to think that the problem could hardly have come up at a more inopportune time for the DOSB.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

It has been revealed that anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

Industry observers note that but Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola noted. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 18:36 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 18:37 EST, 16 November 2026.

Max Dowman broke another record as the 16-year-old became the youngest-ever goalscorer for England's Under-21 side on Monday night.

The Arsenal teenager has already broken a plethora of records at club level, and is now taking that to the international stage too, breaking a record set by senior team star Jude Bellingham, who scored aged 17 years and 67 days in 2020.

Dowman was called into the U21 squad for the first time this international break, and made his debut off the bench in the 1-0 defeat by Portugal on Friday.

On Monday, meanwhile, he was given a start by manager Lee Carsley, and rewarded his manager's faith with an 89th-minute winner to break the record and earn his side a 3-2 win.

It's a record he can add to his already-extensive collection, which includes being the youngest Champions League player, the youngest Premier League goalscorer, and the youngest Premier League winner.

In a recent development, manager Lee Carsley mentioned after the game: 'He played really well - he was one of four or five outstanding performances. Mikey Moore, Max, Ethan (Nwaneri), they were very good.

Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goal scorer when he scored against France on Monday.

'We see how good on the ball he is but he was outstanding off the ball. You have to keep reminding yourself about his age. There's a lot of expectation around him and he seems to handle that so well.

'It's key we keep supporting him and he develops at his own pace. It's so important he enjoys his football.

'Obviously all the players in the squad are under pressure from their clubs and the expectation that surrounds them, so as much as we can we have to make that as easy as we can.'.

Despite bursting onto the scene last season, Dowman has just 19 minutes to his name in the top flight this campaign as Arsenal look to defend their title.

He has played a number of games for the Gunners' U21 side, while he was sent off against League Two side Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup.

Sources indicate that arteta scolded his player at the time, but noted: 'I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction. Whether that's positive or negative. You need to understand the context, the relationship I have with him and what we discussed before we went out.

'If you see the reaction from my mother and father with me sometimes, you'd say "you don't like that reaction", but for me it was the best reaction ever as it enabled me to be who I am.

The Arsenal teenager, 16, broke the record held by Jude Bellingham with his late winner.

'But you want to see the best and most beautiful reaction. You want to see the reaction of his team-mates when they have to play with 10 men.

'What do you expect? That's the level and that's the reaction. Whether it's right or wrong, that's the reaction. And the reaction when I don't win, I'm f****d off, big time.

According to recent reports, 'This is the environment and the reality. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League. We look after him so much but we are also demanding as he needs to earn the right to play otherwise what are the rest of the boys going to tell me?'.

Industry News: Chinese graduate students are now choosing to stay closer to home

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1341 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that hong Kong is expected to have around 35,000 more students from the Chinese mainland enrolled in its higher-education institutions in 2030 than in 2025.
  • Analysis of global higher-education trends indicates that Chinese students are increasingly choosing to stay in Asia to further their studies.
  • According to recent reports, zhao Junyi is one of many postgraduate students who are rerouting back to Asia after studying elsewhere.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that hong Kong is expected to have around 35,000 more students from the Chinese mainland enrolled in its higher-education institutions in 2030 than in 2025. Credit: Vernon Yuen/NurPhoto via Getty.

Analysis of global higher-education trends indicates that Chinese students are increasingly choosing to stay in Asia to further their studies.

According to recent reports, zhao Junyi is one of many postgraduate students who are rerouting back to Asia after studying elsewhere. Originally from Beijing, Zhao started a four-year PhD programme in planetary science at the University of Hong Kong in September. He’s happy about his choice.

In Hong Kong, Zhao says, he can stay abreast of updates from China’s space programme in an English-speaking, international environment, as well as “connect with the research community and collaborate with colleagues from Europe and the United States”.

It has been revealed that hong Kong is a special administrative region of China and has a different education system from the Chinese mainland. Therefore, students from the Chinese mainland studying in Hong Kong are thought of as studying ‘overseas’.

According to recent reports, zhao obtained his bachelor’s degree in astronomy earlier this year from the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor. He notes he decided against furthering his studies in the United States partly because of the federal government’s cuts to scientific funding. He didn’t go back to the Chinese mainland because only those with a master’s degree can apply for doctoral courses there, whereas Hong Kong doesn’t have such a requirement, he explains.

According to recent reports, china’s rapid advancements in space exploration are also a massive draw. Zhao’s current supervisor is analysing lunar samples collected by China’s Chang’e-5 and Chang’e-6 space missions. For Zhao, who grew up as a fan of the Chang’e programme, it is a dream come true to learn about its progress first-hand and to potentially be a part of it himself.

“Hong Kong is so attractive in so many ways,” claims Zhao, who is on a university scholarship that covers his tuition fees, rent and life expenses.

Zhao is among a growing crop of Chinese students who are seeking degrees in Asia rather than in the West.

In a recent development, the shift can be felt most strongly in Malaysia, Hong Kong and Macau. These are the places projected to have the fastest increase in the number of enrolled students from the Chinese mainland between 2025 and 2030, according to figures shared with Nature by London-based consultancy Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), which analyses global higher-education institutions and student mobility (see ‘Student flows’).

It has been revealed that for the wealthy, English-speaking countries that have been popular with Chinese students for decades, the projections by QS point in the opposite direction. The United States, Australia and Canada will see the number of Chinese enrolments decrease year-on-year, with the United Kingdom holding steady. The drop in the number of students headed for the United States is projected to happen particularly quickly.

The trend demonstrates that prospective Chinese students now consider a wider combination of factors, including how far the host country is from home and how easily they can find a job with their degree, says Alice Wei, a consultant at QS.

It has been revealed that for Zhao, one of the most exciting things about studying in Hong Kong is that it means he can visit home easily, especially for important occasions. “I couldn’t go home for the Chinese Newly introduced Year for many years when I was in the United States because it was not a public holiday there.”.

The number of Chinese students studying in US universities is projected to fall by an average of 4% each year between 2025 and 2030, the sharpest drop of all countries and territories assessed.

Students from China — and other countries — are facing more restrictions during and after their time in the United States, Wei says. For example, the US federal government in July proposed putting a hard limit on the duration of visas issued to foreign students and requires them to pack up and leave within 30 days of their programmes ending. Another US proposal suggests a US$100,000 fee for international students if they intend to stay to work after graduating. Australia and Canada have also introduced tougher immigration rules for foreign students.

Recent findings suggest that australia is projected to overtake the United States as the leading study destination for Chinese students by 2030.Credit: Dr. Victor Wong / Shutterstock.

Geopolitical tensions are another deterrent. US-based researchers are increasingly being scrutinized over their collaboration with Chinese partners as the United States enhances research security. For Zhao and other prospective students from China, such efforts make it harder for them to imagine a future in the United States.

Recent findings suggest that “Because I am a Chinese national, it would be nearly impossible for me to participate in NASA’s research programmes,” Zhao says. NASA has blocked Chinese citizens from joining its programme out of security concerns.

Simultaneously, various factors are pulling Chinese students closer to home.

Industry observers note that shorter geographical distances and familiar lifestyles are two possible selling points. Malaysia, for example, is projected to see an annual rise of 13% in the number of Chinese enrolments between 2025 and 2030, the highest growth in QS’s analysis.

Sources indicate that malaysia’s sizeable community of people who speak Mandarin or Chinese dialects makes Chinese students feel at home in the southeast Asian country, says Ngeow Chow Bing, director of the Institute of China Studies at the University of Malaya in Kuala Lumpur. A visa-free travel policy between the two nations also means that their relatives can visit them whenever they want, he says.

It has been revealed that it is hard to compare Chinese students in Malaysia directly with those in the West, because they study different disciplines, Ngeow claims. For example, Chinese students going to the United States are more likely to pursue careers in science, technology, engineering and mathematics, but in Malaysia, the “vast majority” study social sciences and languages, he says. “Malaysia is still not yet very renowned for science and tech,” he notes.

Industry observers note that in South Korea, the fourth fastest-growing destination on the list — with a yearly increase in enrolment rates of 8% — it is the country’s high-tech manufacturing industries that attract Chinese students, such as those for semiconductor chips, biopharmaceutical and advanced materials, says Xie Yuzhen, a Shanghai-based independent researcher who studies China’s higher-education industry. Students can gain first-hand experience in these industries owing to the close relationship between big companies and universities, Xie says.

Junsuk Rho, a materials scientist at Pohang University of Science and Technology in South Korea, has observed an influx of Chinese graduate students to the country over the past few years.

Breaking: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a new study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.
  • Emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change.
  • "It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," remarked the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a new study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

Emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change. While over the past decade, these emissions have risen by 0.9% per year, they are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026.

"It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," remarked the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.

"So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons.".

The study was released while global leaders are meeting in Turkey for the United Nations' COP31 climate conference.

The study published by international research group the Global Carbon Project found that oil emissions dropped by 1.9% in 2026, while natural gas fell by 0.3%. Coal emissions however continued to rise, by around 0.6%.

"A drop in emissions in ‌one year is not a peak unless it ‌is driven ​by structural change," Peters cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that A structural change would mean that emissions would slowly rise to a peak and then slowly decline afterward, indicating a long term trend. That's not what happened though, Peters noted. "What we see this year is [that] oil emissions are going up and then suddenly, bang, down 2%.".

Sources indicate that it is the third time in recent years that global carbon pollution has dropped. The previous declines were during the global economic crisis in 2009 and during the COVID pandemic in 2020. In each of those cases, emissions went back up once global economies recovered.

In a recent development, while the geopolitical shocks of the past year have been the driving factors behind the temporary emissions reversal, there has also been a rise in renewable energy contributing to the data. So while solar panels, wind farms and electric vehicles did make a difference, they were just not enough to cut emissions by themselves.

"The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies," according to co-author of the study, Pierre Friedlingstein, of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University.

And even though emissions from fossil fuels dropped slightly, overall global carbon dioxide emissions still went up by about 1%, the study warns. The overall rise is because of land use changes like deforestation and peat fires, which increased too fast to be offset by the slight decrease in fossil fuel burning.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Has there been a better goalkeeper in the Premier League this season than Leeds United’s James Trafford? It is a question worth asking after his brilliance secured his side a point against Sunderland.

Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.

According to recent reports, after leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds. He is the most expensive British goalkeeper. More importantly, he is playing like it too.

This was a tough examination for Leeds, who were not at their best, against a typically robust and physically challenging Sunderland who are getting back to doing the things that made them so difficult to play against last season. Regis Le Bris’ side created the better chances but were repeatedly denied by Trafford.

With the windy weather playing havoc, ruining the game as a spectacle, as both sides struggled for control of the ball, the two moments of quality came from Trafford in the first half.

Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Industry observers note that trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

It has been revealed that trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

The point means Le Bris’ side have still not won a league game since August and remain bottom of the table. This is proving to be a tougher second season in the top flight for Sunderland, but if they keep playing like this, they will not remain in the bottom three for much longer.

In a recent development, “It’s a positive [point],” stated Le Bris. “The more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.”.

“It’s a positive [point], the more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.

I think we revealed this afternoon that we are in this challenge, we want to embrace it and be ourselves and we probably deserved a bit more today.”.

Sunderland were warned about “second season syndrome” and shrugged them off in the summer as they looked forward to their first European campaign for more than 50 years.

They had dismissed the gloomy pre-season predictions the previous year and had gone on to enjoy their most successful season in the top flight since the heady days of the Peter Reid era at the start of the century.

So when the “experts” told them it would be much harder this season—that they would no longer have the element of surprise and the squad would be badly stretched by the extra games in the Europa League—it was easy to ignore.

You cannot blame them. It has been a magical couple of years on Wearside where everything has gone in their favour, but reality has hit hard this season.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Sunderland and Leeds United at the Stadium of Light.

The final game of this gameweek sees these two Northern giants lock horns once again in a very intriguing encounter, with Sunderland especially in need of three points.

Following their opening season back in the Premier League last term, Sunderland enjoyed a historic campaign, placing seventh to qualify for European competition for the first time in 53 years. Therefore, their workload for the 2025-26 season has increased, which has caused their domestic form to suffer.

Sunderland right now find themselves bottom of the top-flight table, with just one win and four points from their opening seven league matches. They’ve lost their previous four Premier League games, but a win here could lift them out of the drop zone, depending on other results at Old Trafford and Selhurst Park.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, in the Europa League, it’s a completely different story. Regis Le Bris’ side are unbeaten, earning seven points from the first nine available. They drew 1-1 with Polish outfit Lech Poznan on Thursday evening, and given the relentless juggling act of domestic and European football, they’re already back in today against a very well-drilled team.

In a recent development, leeds have made a solid start to the season and find themselves eighth in the Premier League, having only lost one match — a narrow 2-1 defeat to Arsenal at the Emirates earlier this month. Last time out, Daniel Farke’s side drew 1-1 with Manchester United at Elland Road, meaning they’re still searching for a first Premier League win since September 14.

Speaking in his preview, Farke remarked: “To win any point in this league, you always have to be on it. And you always have to be close to be perfect, especially for normal sides - not like the top two. And for that, we are very respectful. So we don’t go into the trap and think we are bigger than we are. We are just the second year back on Premier League level. And we fight for every point.”.

Published: 17:56 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 19:19 EST, 16 November 2026.

Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz scored a stunning brace for Germany as Jurgen Klopp's side thumped the Netherlands in the Nations League.

The 23-year-old has had a tough time of it at Anfield since his £116million move to the club last summer, but has never really struggled on the international stage.

And he continued that trend on Monday evening with two goals for his side to help them top their Nations League group.

Industry observers note that his first was the pick of the bunch. Wirtz moved along the forward line as a Dutch side without Virgil van Dijk struggled to contain him. He picked up the ball around 25 yards out, cut inside onto his weaker left foot, and curled a pearling effort into the far corner off the post.

That goal, which came on the hour mark, put his side 2-0 up after Freiburg's Derry Scherhant had scored the opener, and Wirtz wasn't done there.

Centre back Nico Schlotterbeck made it 3-0 before the Liverpool man picked up his second of the night after drifting into the penalty box unmarked and finishing high after good work from Brajan Gruda.

Industry observers note that cette version de Wirtz avec le maillot de la Mannschaft c’est celle qu’on aimerait voir chaque semaine en PL. Quel missile pour faire le break ! Meilleur buteur allemand sur cette édition de l’UNL. 🇩🇪🔥 pic.twitter.com/m0DqaOungS.

Florian Wirtz scored a brace for Germany as they thumped the Netherlands 5-0 in Nations League action.

Liverpool midfielder Wirtz received a big hug from a smiling Jurgen Klopp at full time.

Gruda himself, who is on loan at RB Leipzig from Brighton, wrapped up the five-star win on a night that arguably saw Klopp announce himself as Germany boss.

After full-time, the ex-Liverpool manager gave Wirtz a huge hug as the duo beamed with big smiles on their faces.

While it was a night to remember for Germany, a Netherlands team that included the likes of Micky van de Ven, Jurrien Timber and Wirtz's Liverpool team-mate Cody Gakpo were left exasperated.

Van Dijk had pulled out of the squad with a knock after playing with a knock in recent weeks.

His side will still, though, compete in the Nations League quarter-finals after finishing second in the group, finishing ahead of Greece on goal difference.

As for Wirtz, he will hope his performance will help continue what has been an uphill climb so far this season.

He also found the net for Germany in their first match of the international break – a 3-1 win over Serbia – and picked up a goal and assist in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break.

In total, he has two goals and five assists in 15 games for Liverpool this season – though the Reds will hope those numbers increase as the season goes on.

His second goal came as he drifted into the penalty area and finished high into the net.

Last month, meanwhile, Reds manager Andoni Iraola insisted he has full faith in his midfielder.

'I think he has had a little bit of everything this season,' he said. 'He has had good games, probably the other day was not his best game, especially offensively. We trust Florian.

'Florian is a very good player. He was coming from good performances in the international break, I think. I think it is a matter of everyone to find his moment.'.

Klopp hailed him 'exceptional', meanwhile, during the last international break.

#25245. Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1001 w)

Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1001 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some 50,000 deaths can be attributed to malnutrition in Germany each year, according to the German Society for Nutritional Medicine (DGEM).
  • The problem is that malnutrition often doesn't become apparent until the consequences are already severe.
  • "In most cases, you don't notice anything at first," noted Matthias Pirlich, a nutritional expert and internal medicine specialist, who once served as DGEM vice president.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some 50,000 deaths can be attributed to malnutrition in Germany each year, according to the German Society for Nutritional Medicine (DGEM).

The problem is that malnutrition often doesn't become apparent until the consequences are already severe.

"In most cases, you don't notice anything at first," noted Matthias Pirlich, a nutritional expert and internal medicine specialist, who once served as DGEM vice president. "You could have a severe vitamin D deficiency for months before any symptoms appear at all. The same applies for vitamin B12. By the time symptoms appear, such as nerve damage, it's already too late.".

A long-term B12 deficiency can damage the spinal cord, leading to numbness in the limbs, muscle weakness or even paralysis. Less common deficiency-related brain damage can cause memory loss and mental health challenges.

All B vitamins play an vital role in metabolism, blood formation and healthy nerve function.

Industry observers note that vitamins, along with various minerals such as calcium, magnesium, iron, iodine and zinc, are classed as micronutrients. The body needs to source them from food, as it cannot produce them itself. Our bodies also need macronutrients like carbohydrates, carbohydrates, protein and fats that provide us with energy.

If the body consumes less food than it needs to maintain all bodily functions over a prolonged period of time, then this is known as undernutrition. A recent World Food Organization (FAO) report estimates that approximately 645 million people worldwide suffer from chronic undernutrition.

Malnutrition, on the other hand, occurs when we consume enough calories but lack certain macronutrients or micronutrients in our food. This, too, can make one sick over time and even prove fatal. About 2 billion people worldwide suffer from this so-called hidden hunger, most of them in the Global South. That noted, even some people in industrialized nations lack crucial micronutrients in their nutrition.

Sources indicate that one study, for instance, found that just under three-quarters of the US population did not meet the recommended daily intake of vitamin D between 2007 and 2010, with more than two-thirds falling short of the recommended amount of vitamin E. And in Germany, about one-third of the population suffered from vitamin D deficiency in 2017, according to the German Nutrition Society. Such deficiency can cause bone, joint and muscle pain. It may also lead to an increased risk of falls and bone fractures.

About one-third of Germans also had an insufficient intake of iodine, a trace element that is indispensable for the production of thyroid hormones. Iodine deficiency can therefore disrupt normal thyroid function. Not only that — during pregnancy, a baby's brain and nervous system can only properly develop with an adequate supply of iodine.

The cultivation of agricultural produce with partially long shelf life or high yields has in some cases caused a decrease in the micronutrient content of fruits, vegetables and grains. Whether this drop in micronutrients is impacting human health, however, is a matter of debate.

Recent findings suggest that malnutrition can result from an unbalanced diet that, while filling and providing energy, lacks essential micronutrients. Examples of such empty calories include fast food and highly processed foods, as well as white bread and white rice.

Poverty is often the reason for such an unbalanced diet, for example when people in the Global South can only afford to buy staples such as flour or rice.

Another study found that in Germany, households at risk of poverty are more likely to consume foods that are low in nutrients and high in calories.

Depression is also associated with an increased risk of nutrient deficiency. "People often lose their appetite, and when they neglect their self-care, they may end up eating a very unbalanced diet," Pirlich told DW. His research indicates that older adults and people who live alone often develop malnutrition, too. The risk also increases the more medications a person takes.

Industry observers note that many diseases result in the body being less efficient at absorbing or utilizing nutrients through the intestines. This applies to people with inflammatory or chronic disease, such as Crohn's disease, celiac disease, liver disease and cancer.

The DGEM estimates that some 30% of all patients receiving inpatient care in Germany are affected by or at risk of malnutrition. Yet health insurance data indicates that only about 1% of patients are screened and treated for nutrient deficiencies.

It has been revealed that often, patients' malnutrition worsens during their hospital stay. The consequences can be serious, potentially causing additional complications, delayed recuperation, longer hospital stays and even increased mortality rates. This results in higher healthcare expenditure, amounting to billions each year.

German policymakers and medical associations are therefore developing a strategy to better screen for and treat malnutrition in hospitals. The road map will be ready by 2027 and copy the Dutch approach in the sense that all patients are checked for nutritional deficiencies upon hospital admission.

Pirlich wants to see such screenings for at-risk groups in outpatient clinics, too: "This includes all those with chronic and serious illnesses and, above all, older adults.".

To prevent poverty-related malnutrition, Pirlich suggests increased access to healthy food, offering free school meals as an example.

The nutritional expert recommends eating a diet that is varied and largely plant-based. "Secondary plant compounds have a very positive effect, and if you eat a highly diverse diet, you consume many different foods that are [nutritionally] beneficial," said Pirlich.

There's a simple rule of thumb: The more colorful your food, the better.

It has been revealed that also, cook vegetables as gently as possible, because overheating and keeping them warm for too long destroys their vitamins. Long storage periods also lead to vitamin loss, so it makes sense to go for seasonal and regional foods in particular.

It has been revealed that but even when ensuring a healthy and balanced diet, some people still develop a nutrient deficiency. A blood test can provide clarity, and dietary supplements may help make up for the deficiency.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Omari Hutchinson insists Milan have ‘got the players’ to challenge for the Scudetto and Europa League, while his dream is to ‘get a contract’ and make the loan move from Nottingham Forest permanent.

The 23-year-old made the transfer on deadline day for €4.2m, with an option to buy at the end of the season for a further €40m.

In case that option is activated, then it would also automatically lead to a contract with the Rossoneri until June 2031.

“It’s going really well, I’m getting my minutes, I still want to push to get into the first team, now we need to start winning more and seeing out games,” Hutchinson told Milan Press as he attended a fan meet and greet in the city.

He is often used as a winger, but was signed on paper to act as a second striker, so where does he prefer?

Sources indicate that “I like to play anywhere, ideally right wing, but wherever the manager puts me, I try to adapt and do my job. He knows what I can do on the ball, he just indicates to create and do your best.”.

There have been some bizarre ups and downs for Milan this season, lurching from success in the Derby della Madonnina to defeat in the Europa League with Ferencvaros in the space of a few days.

“It’s difficult, because we’ve had games where we’re doing well and make silly mistakes. We’ve got to keep pushing on in the Europa League, we’ve got the squad to do it.”.

Hutchinson is certainly enjoying his time at Milan and hopes that it will be a permanent step away from Nottingham Forest.

“I see how passionate everyone is about the club, the fans are always behind you, so it’s amazing to see, because I’ve never had this experience before,” he added.

He has so far contributed one goal and one assist in 11 games between Serie A and the Europa League, but has lofty ambitions for both tournaments.

“We’ve got the players, a good squad, there’s always a small detail that we’re missing, but we’re building on that, the manager and staff are working on it, and once it clicks properly, I think we’ll do well.”.

Hutchinson is only on loan with an option to buy at the end of the season from Nottingham Forest, so he was asked what his dream is.

Industry observers note that “My dream is to do well this season, hopefully get a contract here. I see myself playing here for a little while. The stadium is crazy, you see all the fans, even the away fans, and you want to create special moments to celebrate in front of everyone.”.

Does he see a substantial difference between playing in Serie A and the Premier League?

“I think it’s tough, because when teams play against AC Milan, they want to show their best qualities. Tactically, it’s more defensive in Serie A, maybe you get a little bit more space in the Premier League, but I don’t think there’s a big gap. The leagues are quite close.”.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • International students earn almost 40% of science and engineering PhDs awarded in the United States.Credit: Bill Pugliano/Getty.
  • The number of international students arriving in the United States in August for the start of the academic year has fallen by 28% since 2024, reaching the lowest level since the depths reached in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic.
  • Data from the federal National Travel and Tourism Office show that the number of incoming student-visa holders fell from 387,000 in August 2024 to 277,000 in August 2026 (see ‘Students stay away’).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

International students earn almost 40% of science and engineering PhDs awarded in the United States.Credit: Bill Pugliano/Getty.

The number of international students arriving in the United States in August for the start of the academic year has fallen by 28% since 2024, reaching the lowest level since the depths reached in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Data from the federal National Travel and Tourism Office show that the number of incoming student-visa holders fell from 387,000 in August 2024 to 277,000 in August 2026 (see ‘Students stay away’). The trend has been driven by a decline in the numbers of students from India and China, which dropped by about 50,000 and 23,000, respectively, from 2024 to 2026.

Source: National Travel and Tourism Office (NTTO); Nature analysis.

The number of applications from international students to US PhD programmes has also declined over the past year, falling by 21% from 2025 to 2026, according to a survey of 55 members of the Association of American Universities (AAU), a coalition of research-intensive schools.

These decreases are squeezing already strained university budgets, and researchers worry about the impact on US science. “I can’t imagine a more effective way for the US to cede its dominance in critical scientific fields to China and Europe than by reducing international students,” says Nigel Goldenfeld, a physicist at the University of California, San Diego. In 2024, international students earned 38% of the science and engineering PhDs awarded in the United States.

The great university shake-up: four charts show how global higher education is changing.

The great university shake-up: four charts show how global higher education is changing.

The administration of US President Donald Trump has introduced several restrictions on visas and international travel since Trump took office in early 2025. Last month, the administration also attempted to place a US$100,000 levy on science and engineering students enrolling in extended Optional Practical Training (OPT), a work programme used by hundreds of thousands of recent graduates and the largest pipeline of scientific talent into the United States. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which issued the proposal, stated that it is meant to “combat fraud, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system, and protect U.S. workers”.

Recent findings suggest that federal judges have suspended the OPT charge and other efforts that the administration made to curb immigration. But higher-education specialists link these attempts to the large decrease in new overseas students, who, they say, can no longer count a US education as a stable investment. “Uncertainty has become policy, and that has registered in the hearts and minds of students,” notes Chris Glass, a higher-education researcher at Boston College in Massachusetts.

The United Kingdom, Canada and Australia have also seen drops in enrolment of international students after placing upcoming limits on these populations. But the US policies are especially restrictive, Glass says.

A spokesperson for the White House did not respond to Nature’s request for comment.

Bruno Fernandes has been dropped for Manchester United’s crucial Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Michael Carrick has taken the decision to drop the United captain to the bench in the wake of his public criticism on Wednesday following the shambolic 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como.

Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics and has now been taken out of the starting XI.

The move had looked likely with Carrick refusing to rule out stripping Fernandes of the captaincy when quizzed on the matter on Friday.

Carrick had responded to Fernandes questioning the set up and approach by suggesting tactics can go out of the window when players are unprepared to run.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Manchester United vs Bouremouth.

United enter Sunday’s clash against Bournemouth in the grip of a deepening crisis. Wednesday night’s dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat to debutants Como extended United’s’ winless run to seven matches across all competitions - their worst sequence since 2015.

Industry observers note that with just one victory from their opening seven Premier League fixtures, United are enduring their worst start to a top-flight season since 1986-87. Head coach Michael Carrick, a multiple champion at Old Trafford during his playing days, finds his position under severe threat, with reports suggesting another defeat could seal his departure. While both of United’s wins this season have come at home, they remain winless in their last three at Old Trafford. On an individual level, Bryan Mbeumo has offered a rare bright spark, scoring four goals in seven league outings while Bruno Fernandes continues to search for form, and the captain’s recent outburst only makes the atmosphere more febrile.

Sources indicate that in stark contrast, Bournemouth arrive in Manchester brimming with confidence. Marco Rose’s side have enjoyed a flawless start to their inaugural European campaign, sitting joint-top of the Europa League standings after a dominant 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s ten-man AC Milan on Thursday. That result marked a third consecutive home win and clean sheet, with Bournemouth outscoring opponents 8-0 in that stretch. Midfielder Marcus Tavernier has been instrumental, leading the club’s scoring charts with five goals across 11 appearances.

Sources indicate that bournemouth will feel no trepidation visiting Old Trafford, having gone unbeaten in their last six Premier League meetings with United (two wins, four draws). With Carrick desperate for a stabilising result and Rose’s side riding high on European momentum, today’s fixture carries significant stakes for both clubs.

Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In its role as president of negotiations at the UN climate talks in Turkey, Australia is being pressured to guide nations toward unified action on slashing the greenhouse gas emissions that are generated in large part by burning fossil fuels.
  • The nation has pledged to lead by example at the summit through a strong commitment to renewable energy, electrification and reduced reliance on planet-heating coal, oil and gas.
  • "Renewable energy, grids, storage and electrification are creating opportunities to strengthen resilience, improve energy security, and reduce emissions at the same time," said Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister, in October during a meeting in Fiji ahead of the COP climate conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In its role as president of negotiations at the UN climate talks in Turkey, Australia is being pressured to guide nations toward unified action on slashing the greenhouse gas emissions that are generated in large part by burning fossil fuels.

The nation has pledged to lead by example at the summit through a strong commitment to renewable energy, electrification and reduced reliance on planet-heating coal, oil and gas.

"Renewable energy, grids, storage and electrification are creating opportunities to strengthen resilience, improve energy security, and reduce emissions at the same time," said Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister, in October during a meeting in Fiji ahead of the COP climate conference.

"These are proven, commercial and scalable today. Now is the moment for faster implementation.".

Yet Australia is also the world's third-largest exporter of fossil fuels. And unlike France and Germany, or island nations from Fiji to the Bahamas that are highly vulnerable to a changing climate, the COP31 co-president has not yet committed to phasing them out.

As calls grow for the country to set a clear route to a clean energy future, critics say its vague promise to transition away from polluting sources of power does not go far enough.

Australia is home to 56% of the world's coal mine projects currently in the pipeline, notes environmental nonprofit, 350.org.

Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at the organization, is calling on the country, the world's second-largest coal exporter, to reverse course and announce an "overdue coal phaseout date" during the COP31 conference.

"Australia needs to walk the walk and follow Germany's example and commit to a phaseout," said Melanie Pill, founder of The Climate Project, an Australia-based climate policy advisory.

The argument to end fossil fuel production is not only about cutting emissions but reducing dependence on energy systems that rely on volatile oil and gas markets, she explained.

"A fossil phaseout in the face of the enduring and escalating conflict in the Middle East is in the interest of everyone," Pill told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

This is especially true for Australia's diesel-reliant Pacific neighbors, who spend up to 25% of GDP on fossil fuel imports — as opposed 6% on health — according to a report by the Institute for Climate Risk and Response at the University of New South Wales.

As lead negotiator at the UN climate talks, Australia can "flip the narrative" on a fossil fuel phaseout, using the challenge of energy security as a justification, mentioned Pill.

This opportunity could be lost, however, if Australia fails to address fossil fuel exports that accounted for 80% of its total carbon footprint in 2022 — and near 5% of global emissions.

While the nation is a world leader in rooftop solar, and generates around half of its electricity from renewables, this progress is "being undone by its continued approval of more fossil fuels for export," remarked Simon Bradshaw, COP31 lead and climate expert at Greenpeace Australia Pacific.

He noted that the Labor government of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has approved the construction, expansion or extension of 38 coal, oil and gas projects since coming to power four years ago on a pro-climate platform.

"You cannot aspire to lead on climate abroad if you're not getting your own house in order," mentioned Thomas Houlie, climate and energy policy analyst at Climate Analytics, a global climate policy institute.

In 2025, when Australia approved the extension of a major gas export project in the country's west until 2070, Albanese justified the move in the name of a balance between "security of energy supply" and "support [for] the transition which reduces our emissions.".

The country has publicly backed a global transition away from the fossil fuels driving the global temperature rise linked to extreme heat and drought. Both through the Global Stocktake agreed at the 2023 UN climate summit, and via the inaugural "transitioning away" summit in Colombia this April, at which Australia and 56 countries pledged to develop a fossil fuel exit road map.

But these commitments are not reflected in Australian resources policy, or its domestic rollout of clean power infrastructure.

"While the government has set a renewables target for electricity, it leaves plenty of blind spots in other sectors," said Houlie, adding that emission reductions in industry and transport have been limited and that the push to achieve an 82% renewables target for the electricity grid by 2030 is behind schedule.

In its role as lead negotiator at COP31, Australia has promised to ensure that any final conference text serves to "elevate the views and the experiences" of small Pacific nations in its region, from Vanuatu to Tuvalu.

These island countries that generate low emissions yet suffer extreme climate impacts from worsening cyclones or rising seas are "sick of Australia's double talk on climate," said Shiva Gounden, head of Pacific at Greenpeace Australia Pacific.

Australia must commit to "substantial fresh funding contributions" to help Pacific neighbors adapt to the climate emergency and achieve energy independence, said his colleague Bradshaw. He reiterated the need to concurrently create a "national road map" away from coal and gas production and export.

A Climate Analytics report co-authored by Houlie outlines a fossil fuel phaseout pathway for Australia that can begin immediately. This includes an end to coal power generation by 2034 and a rapid reduction in oil and gas consumption, with renewables generating almost all the country's electricity by 2040. Fossil fuel export projects would be eliminated, and existing ones shuttered before becoming obsolete.

"This co-presidency is a golden opportunity for Australia to step up and commit to a phaseout," said Houlie.

Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the new manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'.

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'.

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker.

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season.

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

According to recent reports, 'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

Industry observers note that '(De Ligt has) got one significant problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'.

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

According to recent reports, 'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

According to recent reports, 'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

Industry observers note that 'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'.

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville noted. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

In a recent development, 'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'.

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in fresh head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt.

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month.

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come promptly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

Sources indicate that 'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's strategy for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

Sources indicate that 'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'.

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

Sources indicate that ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

Sources indicate that ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

Sources indicate that ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.
